items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: So we had Bob Schottman to stand over me, the whole time in between the pitches.

ctx.x: But you watch the stick. And I see a lot of fellas that used to get out there in the deep, we call it out in the deep water, and they call WP Pound Plenty, and things like that. But when he do this, that means give y'all triple 40, and then you see him, one of those things, for sound, you know, boom, you know. And just like a double P, you start off, you know, and you get to, when you get to the, to your top volume, well you just come right on back to where you started, you know. It's a term for that. And so he…
So when you started playing music, you just went into music professionally, you didn't have any other profession.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And Joe gets Bob Shottley, Tick Gray, the fellas, and goes in the plantation.

ctx.x: But Lee never did talk about it?

No, well that's what happened. Well Lee was playing there, he was playing there with Rudy and Nichols and his boys, they were playing together there. And then Joe was on the drums. And Joe lived right there at 31st Estate. Joe was teaching this boy, this Italian boy, I call his name. Penico? Yeah, he was teaching Penico. Yeah, he was teaching Penico. And Joe, he'd be taking a whole lot of time up with them young musicians, time with him, I mean as far as teaching them and telling them this and telling them that…
Oh Tick Gray, is that any relation to the union president?
